messages:
Elaine (AE): Quick thread — Customer (FinEdge) wants Private deployment POC. Key asks: preserve client src IP, deterministic failover to alternate region, and zero outbound IP changes for compliance. Any blockers?
Ryan (NetOps): Quick Q — are they open to using PrivateLink (interface endpoint) + our egress proxy, or do they insist on VPC peering/transit? PrivateLink preserves client IP only if the connector is deployed in-customer?
Elaine (AE): They prefer PrivateLink for least network change, but legal insists on source-ip visibility in backend logs. They also mentioned they have strict firewall rules allowing only a small port range.
Devon (Solutions): TL;DR: PrivateLink -> traffic terminates at our connector endpoint. Source IP seen by customer's backend depends on topology: if they route through a customer-managed proxy before PrivateLink, srcIP preserved; if our connector SNATs to an EIP, srcIP is not preserved.
Ryan (NetOps): If they want true srcIP preservation we can recommend: deploy our connector in their VPC (Private deployment) so packets originate from within their network. Alternative is to use a passthrough L4 proxy in their account and forward to our PrivateLink. Both require firewall rules for 443 + optional health/metrics ports.
Anya (SE): Adding port checklist for their firewall: 443 (TLS) outbound to our PrivateLink ENIs; 10250 (metrics) optional; 123/ntp only if they permit time sync. If they use a TCP proxy, also allow ephemeral ports 32768-61000 for backend-to-proxy.
Elaine (AE): Cost question from procurement: how much more for Private deployment vs Dedicated? any one-off infra/setup fees for deploying our connector into customer VPC?
Devon (Solutions): Pricing notes: Private deployment has a platform license + infra uplift (one-time deployment engineering + monthly connector fee). If they host connector in their VPC, infra cost to them is just the instance/GW cost. We bill support+license. I'll pull exact numbers but estimate ~1.2x hosted per-token unit for small POC (covers dedicated connector infra).
Ryan (NetOps): Failover design: recommend active/active across two AZs + route health checks. For region fallback, use TGW/transit or DNS-based failover pointing to secondary PrivateLink endpoints. Important: healthcheck TTLs must be conservative.
Anya (SE): Note: SNI passthrough matters — if their firewall does TLS inspection, SNI may be stripped. Recommend allowing TLS passthrough for our hostnames or register their inspection appliance to trust our certs.
Elaine (AE): Security questionnaire section: they asked for a short snippet we can paste under "Network Architecture for Private Deployment". Anyone have a concise copy-paste answer?
Devon (Solutions): Paste below (short):
```
Network Architecture for Private Deployment: Redwood connector can be deployed into the customer's VPC. Communication between in-VPC connector and Redwood control plane is over TLS (443) to configured egress endpoints. For preserved client IPs, deploy connector within the customer's subnets and configure route tables to send application traffic via the connector. Required firewall openings: outbound 443 to Redwood control plane EIPs and inbound 443 to connector ENIs if using interface endpoints. For failover, use DNS-based endpoint switching or TGW route priorities. No proprietary protocols required; standard TLS-based HTTP/TCP traffic only.
```
Ryan (NetOps): Small config snippet for their infra team (example SG):
```
# allow outbound to Redwood control plane
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-xxxx --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 203.0.113.0/24
# allow connector inbound for app traffic
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-connector --protocol tcp --port 443 --source-group sg-app
```
Anya (SE): Also flag: if they need source IP preservation for geolocation / fraud detection, confirm whether logs are read at the app or at a shared LB — LB may still rewrite srcIP.
Elaine (AE): OK. Next steps: I'll send the short security answer to procurement, ask legal whether they accept connector-in-VPC. Can someone prepare a one-page diagram for the POC showing PrivateLink vs connector-in-VPC?
Devon (Solutions): I'll draft the diagram + a cost appendix. Ryan, can you add the exact EIP ranges we use for control-plane egress so they can align firewall allowlist?
Ryan (NetOps): Yep — will send ranges and a minimal HLD in the next 2 hrs. I'll also note recommended healthcheck TTLs and DNS failover steps.
deploy-bot: POC environment created: redwood-poc-finedge-2026, id poc-ff12ab. Docs link: https://internal.redwood/pocs/poc-ff12ab
Elaine (AE): Perfect, thanks all :tada:
Devon (Solutions): I'll DM the diagram when ready.
Anya (SE): Ping me on any deep packet or TLS inspect questions.
Elaine (AE): Closing the loop — I'll post updates in the sales playbook thread once we've heard back from FinEdge legal.
